```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(rio)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(janitor)
library(knitr)
library(psych)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
```

### The dataset ###
```{r}
d <- read_sav(here("outcomes paper/data_outcomes", "p_y_w1_for_analysesjan25_2.sav")) # 94 rows

d1 <- d %>%
  select(all_of(c(
    "school_id", "family_id", "participant_id", "parent_eng_comf", "youth_age", "youth_gender",
    "acadhwi_1", "checkhwi_1", "struct_1", "knowschool_1", 
    "stratsbi_1", "belong_1", "endorse_1", "ptrel_1", "selfeffic_1",
    "y_sch_eng", "grades"
  )))

d2 <- d1 %>%
  mutate(parent_eng_comf = as.numeric(parent_eng_comf),
         youth_gender = factor(youth_gender),
         youth_age = as.numeric(youth_age))
```

### Select and rename requested variables for readability ###
```{r}
meta_vars <- d2[, c("selfeffic_1",
                    "y_sch_eng",
                    "grades",
                    "stratsbi_1",
                    "acadhwi_1",
                    "checkhwi_1")]

colnames(meta_vars) <- c(
  "EFFICACY",
  "ENGAGE",
  "GRADES",
  "PROA",
  "HWI 1",
  "HWI 2"
) # following abbreviated name convention in paper Garcia Isaza et al. (2026)
```

### Pearson correlation matrix ###
```{r}
cor(meta_vars, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
```

### Sample sizes for each pairwise correlation ###
```{r}
corr.test(meta_vars, use = "pairwise")$n
```
